Title: Egyptian mummies coming to Sarawak next year
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak is set to host a major international exhibition featuring artefacts and actual human remains dating back over 5,000 years from the National Archaeological Museum of Florence, Italy, next year.
Sarawak Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the exclusive six-month exhibition, titled 'Egyptian Mummies: Journey Towards Immortality', will be held at the Borneo Cultures Museum (BCM) starting July next year.
"This is a first for Southeast Asia. Collaborations between museums for exhibitions of this kind usually take a long time.
"Because it's already difficult to bring in the exhibits and if you want to do it for a month, it's a loss. So we will do it for six months, and it will be a totally new attraction to locals," he said in a press conference after winding up the debate for his ministry at the Sarawak state legislative assembly sitting today.
He said the Sarawak Museum Department's success in bringing in such a global-scale exhibition demonstrates the agency's capability and proactive approach in establishing strategic collaborations with world-renowned museums.
Meanwhile, in his winding up speech, Abdul Karim highlighted that Sarawak's overall tourism sector has staged a remarkable growth trajectory, recording 3.52 million visitor arrivals and generating RM9 billion in tourism receipts between January and September 2026.
"Asean remains our major market, with Brunei and Indonesia accounting for 46.5 per cent of visitors, while Singapore, the Philippines and Thailand also contributed significantly to our visitor arrivals," he said.

Title: ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent place over US$35bil worth of Nvidia chip orders
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than three million of Nvidia's new RTX PRO 5500 graphics cards with a collective sticker price of over US$35 billion, two people familiar with the matter said, in a rush for a less powerful but export-compliant chip amid US restrictions on trade with China.
US-based chipmaker Nvidia has told customers and partners it cannot guarantee that it can fill the orders because demand from Chinese technology companies far exceeds planned production, the two sources and a third person familiar with the matter said. They requested anonymity because they are not authorised to speak to the media.
The RTX PRO 5500 is a workstation chip, designed for powerful professional computers rather than the large data-centre clusters that use Nvidia's most advanced AI processors. But it is among the most powerful Nvidia chips that are still available to Chinese buyers.
Nvidia's Blackwell-based B300 data-centre chip is not allowed to be sold to Chinese buyers under US export controls, while exports of its Hopper-based H200 are reviewed on a case-by-case basis and are subject to licensing conditions.
One source said Nvidia told partners they might receive only five per cent to 10 per cent of the quantities requested. Another said the company had indicated it could produce no more than 3 million RTX PRO 5500 cards globally in 2027. Total orders from customers in China have exceeded 6 million, two of the sources said.
The three Chinese tech giants' orders are for cards priced at about US$11,400 each, two of the sources said, giving them a potential combined value of more than US$35 billion.
The scale of the orders, which have not been previously reported, underscores the ongoing appetite among Chinese companies for Nvidia hardware despite the US curbs.
Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang has said the restrictions reduced Nvidia's share of China's AI data-centre chip market from a near monopoly to effectively nothing. But demand for the RTX PRO 5500 suggests Nvidia retains a sizeable potential market in China through less powerful products that may still be available.
The surge in demand also highlights how US restrictions have tightened computing-power supplies in the world's second-largest economy as Chinese companies race to develop cutting-edge AI models and propel Beijing's effort to deploy the technology across its industries.
Washington's curbs have pushed Chinese firms toward domestic suppliers, while Beijing has encouraged the use of homegrown chips.
Huawei, in particular, has gained market share, though Chinese chipmakers have generally struggled to match leading American products, partly because separate restrictions have limited access to the foreign equipment that is used to make the most advanced semiconductors.
An Nvidia spokesperson said Chinese producers of workstation chips and cards have experienced "unprecedented growth since 2022," when the curbs were first imposed.
"US firms continue to be restricted by a combination of outdated US export controls, which cover gaming products released nearly a half a decade ago, and China's own limit on US imports," the spokesperson said.
ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent did not respond to requests for comment.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees the export controls, and China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology did not respond to requests for comment.
AN EXPORT-COMPLIANT ALTERNATIVE
The RTX PRO 5500 is less powerful than Nvidia's H200 and B300 chips, which are designed to be linked in large numbers for the most demanding AI training and deployment workloads.
Chinese companies are seeking to use the cards primarily for AI inference, or running trained models to generate chatbot responses, the three sources said. Inference generally requires less computing power than training models on massive datasets.
The RTX PRO 5500 is similar to the RTX 6000D in performance, according to product specifications seen by Reuters.
Nvidia launched the RTX 6000D in the middle of last year as a reduced-capability product designed to meet US export restrictions. Major Chinese tech firms initially showed little interest, with some declining to place orders, Reuters reported last year.
At the time, buyers viewed the chips as overly expensive given their capabilities and hoped Washington would eventually allow sales of more powerful Nvidia processors.
Those expectations have faded as restrictions have remained in place and AI computing capacity has remained scarce, making the RTX PRO 5500 a more attractive substitute, two of the sources said.
SUPPLY SQUEEZE
Nvidia's inability to promise full deliveries reflects both a surge in demand and its manufacturing priorities, two of the sources said.
Starting in 2027, Nvidia is expected to devote much of its capacity at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co to Rubin, its next-generation platform for large-scale data centres, rather than products like the RTX PRO 5500, two of the sources said. TSMC declined to comment.
Nvidia has told customers to expect early samples in December, with commercial deliveries beginning in the first quarter of 2027, they added.
The RTX 6000D has since been discontinued and its market price in China has doubled, one of the sources said.
In an Oct 13 filing, Shenzhen-listed fintech and AI-computing services company Tansun Technology said it had agreed to buy 20,000 RTX PRO 5500 cards from an unidentified counterparty.
It cautioned that supply shortages, industry demand and overseas technology controls could delay deliveries or reduce volumes.

Title: 16-year-old girl rescued from suspected sex exploitation in Arau
Article:
KANGAR: Police rescued a 16-year-old girl suspected of being sexually exploited by a prostitution syndicate through a social media application during a raid at a premises in Arau yesterday.
Perlis police chief Deputy Commissioner Hamzah Hashim said two men were also arrested during the raid under Op Noda at 11.15pm.
He said the arrests and rescue were carried out following police intelligence and information about prostitution activities involving the sexual exploitation of children in the area.
"During the raid, police arrested the two men, who are suspected of promoting prostitution through the MiChat application and sexually exploiting the victim.
"The case is being investigated under Section 14 of the Anti-Trafficking in Persons and Anti-Smuggling of Migrants Act 2007 (ATIPSOM). If convicted, the accused face life imprisonment or a minimum jail term of five years, and may also be caned," he said in a statement today.
Hamzah said the case was also being investigated under Section 372(1)(e) of the Penal Code, which provides for imprisonment of up to 15 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

Title: Ministry, UM have no plans to act against student rep over 'tough' question - Zambry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Higher Education Ministry and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a "tough" question during the i-Future programme.
Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the ministry maintained its position that students' right to freedom of expression must be respected, while condemning any form of abuse, insults or threats directed at the student on social media.
"My position is clear. Respect students' right to speak up. As we have stated, amendments to the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) have provided them with the space to express their views.
"This freedom should also be exercised responsibly, courteously and based on facts," he said in a statement shared on TikTok today.
Earlier, a video lasting more than two minutes went viral, showing a Universiti Malaya Students' Union representative firmly questioning a panel during a dialogue session held as part of the i-Future programme.
The student, among other things, expressed concerns about the integrity of leadership and criticised the collection of public donations to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine imposed as one of the conditions for allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence for the SRC International case under
house arrest
.
Commenting on allegations of threats, abuse and condemnation
directed at the student
, Zambry said such behaviour should not occur and advised the student to lodge a police report to enable an investigation.
He urged the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to examine the posts and accounts involved, including the possibility that fake accounts had been used.
"If anyone has attempted to engage in wrongdoing, the student concerned should take appropriate action by lodging a report with the relevant authorities," he said.
Zambry urged all parties not to politicise the issue or exploit students to advance specific agendas.
"I also urge everyone not to turn students into weapons of political propaganda, to the extent that they become victims of certain agendas.
"For example, some ministers have even called for shirts, T-shirts and the like to be made, whereas at the ministry level, we have absolutely no intention of taking any action against the student concerned," he said.
The student,
Ummi Umairah Bakhit
, said she would not retract her remarks about public donations to Najib, made at a summit recently.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM: TuJu offers local alternative for road navigation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is encouraging the public to use TuJu, a locally developed navigation application created by the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA), as an alternative for road navigation.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the alternative was proposed due to security concerns over information and data on citizens' movements, given that the Waze application is subject to Israeli laws.
He said the matter was among the topics discussed at the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee, which he chaired today to review evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation's preparedness and digital sovereignty.
"Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).
"We cannot compromise when it comes to the security of our citizens' data and identities. Therefore, the government is strengthening an integrated identity ecosystem utilising MyKad as a physical credential and MyDigital ID for digital transactions, supported by more robust cyber protections, including preparations for future threats via PQC," he said in a Facebook post.
The prime minister said these efforts were crucial to ensuring that the digitalisation of public services continued to benefit the people without compromising security, public trust or national sovereignty.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: i-City unveils AI-powered homes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: i-City has launched AI Living @ i-City, a residential concept combining home automation, robotics, wellness technology and artificial intelligence (AI), with its first development comprising 500 units.
The development, centred on the i-Ris residential tower, is designed to accommodate domestic robots through layouts, circulation paths, service areas and infrastructure planned around their use alongside residents.
At the centre of the concept is i-Ris, an AI companion intended to help residents control home functions and access authorised technologies and services based on their needs and preferences.
The developer is rolling out a digital marketing campaign from October 2026 to introduce the concept to prospective homebuyers, ahead of the planned opening of a residence showroom at the AI World Experience Centre (AIWEC) in January 2027.
Datuk Firdaus, chairman of Firdaus & Associates (the development's lead marketing agency), said the campaign aims to explain how AI and robotics could be incorporated into residential living, including home security, elderly care and lifestyle management.
Savills Malaysia group managing director Datuk Sr Paul Khong said AI-based services and robotics could become another factor influencing homebuyers' property choices, alongside location, design, facilities and price.
AI Living builds on i-City's technology-focused development, which includes AIWEC, established in collaboration with Chinese robotics company AgiBot.
The centre showcases more than 100 robots in interactive settings.
i-City chairman Tan Sri Lim Kim Hong said the concept reflects the developer's view that homes would increasingly use technology to respond to residents' needs.
The planned showroom will allow prospective buyers to explore selected features of the concept and learn more about the i-Ris development.
However, the developer has yet to disclose the residential units' prices or provide details on the costs of maintaining and upgrading the technology over time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: LYC Healthcare appeals against delisting
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: LYC Healthcare Bhd has appealed against the commencement of delisting proceedings, putting its scheduled removal from Bursa Malaysia on hold pending the exchange's decision.
In a bourse filing today, the healthcare services provider said it submitted the appeal on Oct 20, ahead of the Oct 26 deadline.
The appeal follows the termination of its advisory relationship with UOB Kay Hian (M) Sdn Bhd, leaving the company without a sponsor for its proposed Guidance Note 3 regularisation plan.
LYC Healthcare is scheduled to be delisted from the ACE Market on Oct 29, while trading in its securities is due to be suspended from Oct 27.
The company said the delisting would be deferred pending Bursa Malaysia's decision on the appeal.
"Given that the appeal was submitted within the appeal timeframe (on or before Oct 26), the removal of the securities of the companyfrom the official list of Bursa Malaysia on Oct 29 shall be deferred pending the decision by Bursa Malaysia on the appeal," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTD warns of fake TikTok account offering driving licences without tests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has confirmed that a TikTok account using the name Ahmad Mushidi, which offers driving licences without requiring applicants to sit for tests, is fake.
The RTD said it had received complaints about advertisements on the social media platform offering driving licences without the need to attend classes or undergo driving tests.
Following the complaints, the department lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
"The public is advised not to be easily deceived by advertisements or unauthorised accounts offering such services to avoid confusion and financial losses.
"Any enquiries or announcements regarding RTD services should be made through the department's official platforms only," it said in a statement on its official Facebook page.
A check of the TikTok account found that it was offering Class B2 motorcycle licences for RM350 and full Class B (B Full) motorcycle licences for RM380, without requiring applicants to sit for RTD tests.
The comments section of the videos also showed users expressing interest in obtaining the services.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 13 killed, 34 injured as truck crashes into tour bus in Egypt
Article:
GIZA: A large truck crashed into a tour bus west of the Egyptian capital on Tuesday, killing 13 people and injuring 34, state media reported.
The Al-Ahram newspaper said "13 individuals were killed and 34 others injured in the tragic collision between the bus and the truck on the Cairo-Asyut Western Desert Road."
An AFP correspondent reported that authorities were clearing the highway. A crane lifted the large bus, the entire front section of which was ripped off, leaving behind mangled steel and debris.
Passenger seats were scattered by the roadside, while debris from the bus was visible on the rear of the truck.
Al-Ahram reported that the injured were receiving treatment at a hospital in Giza, and an investigation was underway to determine the cause of the crash.
Road accidents are common in Egypt and are often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance and uneven law enforcement.
Last year, nearly 6,000 people were killed in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt's state statistics agency.
Last month, a bus crash in Sinai killed 22 people, including 10 Jordanian tourists.
In August, at least 18 people, many of them children, were killed in northern Egypt when two pick-up trucks carrying agricultural day-labourers crashed.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver detained after dangerous overtaking in Johor Baru [WATCH]
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 38-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of endangering other road users by driving dangerously on Jalan Bakawali, Taman Johor Jaya.
Seri Alam deputy police chief Superintendent Victor Genason said the man was detained at 9.35am at the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division of the Seri Alam district police headquarters.
He said the arrest followed the circulation of a 34-second video on Facebook.
"The video shows a car overtaking other vehicles dangerously on the road and has garnered about 43,000 views," he said in a statement today.
Victor said police also seized a Proton e.MAS believed to have been used by the man during the incident.
He added that an initial urine screening test found the suspect negative for drugs.
The case is being investigated under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for reckless and dangerous driving.
Police advised the public to obey traffic laws and drive responsibly to ensure everyone's safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Schools in six states, KL and Putrajaya to operate as usual tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In NEGRI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MOE) would operate as usual.
However, the Final Academic Session Exam (UASA) scheduled during this period must be postponed and rescheduled by the respective schools.
The postponement also applies to all internal school examinations, in line with the MOE's statement dated Oct 15. All outdoor activities must be suspended if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100.
In MELAKA, SELANGOR, PUTRAJAYA and KUALA LUMPUR, school administrators were instructed to monitor API readings issued by the Department of Environment and pay particular attention to pupils at higher risk.
In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.
Schools in other districts would operate as usual, with any changes to be announced through the respective district education offices.
The PERAK Education Department urged everyone to remain alert to developments and heed the authorities' advice on the haze.
In PENANG, the state Education Department encouraged pupils to drink sufficient water and instructed schools to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water.
Pupils and school staff are also encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
The education departments in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Perak and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, have also given parents and guardians who are concerned about their children's health the option of keeping them at home, provided they inform the school.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek was reported as saying that decisions on
school closures
due to haze were made jointly by the Education Ministry, Health Ministry and Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on their respective areas of expertise.
She said the decisions took into account air quality monitoring and health risks to students, as well as the impact on learning if schools were closed for too long.
Meanwhile,  Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, called on the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive steps and
collective action
to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and their families.
In a royal message posted on the official Facebook page of Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar last night, Her Majesty also emphasised community cooperation in strengthening Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR), as well as long-term strategic planning to deal with haze.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four states record highest rates of drug abuse - Nada
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (NADA) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 people per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646).
"The ranking of these four states reflects the extent of drug addiction and abuse that requires attention and targeted intervention.
"Geographical factors also contribute to this situation, with cross-border smuggling routes identified as among the risk factors influencing drug-related problems in these areas," he said in a statement today.
Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.
He said the statistics were compiled based on integrated data from four main sources, namely Nada, the police, Health Ministry and private rehabilitation centres.
In this regard, Ruslin said Nada was focusing on enforcement, prevention programmes and community empowerment in high-risk states, targeting three main segments, namely, educational institutions, families and communities.
"A total of 242 prevention and public awareness programmes were conducted, involving 16,408 participants overall, including 228 programmes in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah, which involved more than 16,000 participants," he said.
He added that 4,253 enforcement operations had been conducted nationwide, with 30,157 people detained for treatment and rehabilitation programmes as of last Sunday.
On treatment and rehabilitation, Ruslin said Nada prioritised a voluntary approach, with the average number of people seeking treatment on their own initiative rising from 75 a month in 2025 to 232 a month this year.
"This increase reflects positive progress following the implementation of amendments to the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, which came into force on Aug 22, 2025," he said.
He said Nada would continue to adopt a data-driven approach and strengthen cooperation with state governments through the Drug Eradication Action Council (MTMD) meetings to coordinate prevention, treatment and rehabilitation efforts involving various agencies, families, educational institutions and communities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man charged over attack on Australian MP Haines
Article:
MELBOURNE: Australian police charged a man on Tuesday over what they alleged was a "targeted" attack with a vehicle on independent lawmaker Helen Haines.
Haines is fighting for her life in a hospital in Melbourne after being struck on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, just over 200km northeast of the Victoria state capital.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has led an outpouring of support for Haines, who was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.
Her attack has also sparked soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare but where police have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards the nation's elected officials in recent years.
The independent lawmaker, 65, was getting things from the trunk of her car when she was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser on Monday afternoon.
The driver had made a U-turn to get back to her after passing, Albanese said on Tuesday.
"It's clear this was a deliberate act," he said.
- 'TARGETED' ATTACK -
Haines was critically injured and underwent surgery overnight at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne.
National broadcaster ABC and The Sydney Morning Herald said that she had lost a leg, with reports indicating she was fighting to keep the other.
The 43-year-old male driver of the vehicle has been identified by Australian media and was reportedly known to police.
He was charged on Tuesday evening with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison.
"Police will allege the incident was targeted," Victoria police said.
The man will appear in court in Wangaratta on Wednesday, they said.
A statement released by the charged man's parents said Haines had been their friend for more than two decades and described Monday's events as "devastating and unfathomable", The Age newspaper reported.
"We would like to sincerely thank members of the local community and police who came to Helen's aid yesterday after the shocking and horrific crime," the statement said.
The alleged attacker was restrained by local barber Ricky Jefferies, now widely hailed as a "hero."
Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: "My wife would be disappointed if I'm injured."
"My family, they're everything, and my community is second to that," a visibly shaken Jefferies told journalists.
"The other people here were just, they did so much more than me... they deserve the credit."
- TOO HEATED -
The alleged attacker's motive remains unknown and Albanese has refused to speculate while the investigation takes place.
But he has bemoaned the fact that political debate in Australia had grown too heated and personal over the past few years.
"It's important in a democracy that people are allowed to have disagreements," he said.
"But that doesn't mean that you have to draw into question people's motivations or their patriotism or who they are."
"We've seen, I think, political discourse go in the wrong direction in recent times," he said.
Australia's spy agency chief Mike Burgess said "elevated levels of grievance, intolerance and polarisation continue to create a permissive environment of violence."
Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action.
Tributes to her have poured in from across the political spectrum.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Selangor steps up monitoring of Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The Selangor government is stepping up efforts to monitor the spread of Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings in the state through the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais), in cooperation with mosques and surau.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the efforts also included educating the public on the differences between Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings and the beliefs of Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah, an initiative that had been ongoing for years.
"Mosques and surau play an important role in promptly contacting Jais if they detect any suspicious activities related to Islam.
"We also organise large-scale programmes to explain the differences between Ahmadiyah or Qadiani teachings and the practices of Ahli Sunnah Wal Jamaah," he told reporters after the launch of a collaboration involving Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), Universiti Selangor (Unisel) and the Selangor Technical Skills Development Centre (STDC) here today.
On Oct 17, the media reported that
two premises in Kampung Nakhoda and Kampung Laksamana
, Gombak, one of which was raided by the authorities, were believed to have been used by foreigners as centres for Ahmadiyah Qadiani teachings.
The premises were reportedly not authorised by the Selangor Islamic Religious Council to conduct Friday prayers and were believed to have been used by foreigners, suspected to be from Pakistan, as gathering places to spread the teachings.
Yesterday, Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said his office would seek further information on developments in the case involving the detention of 288 individuals linked to the teachings in Sabah.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'I thought he was surrendering': Cop recounts parang attack [WATCH]
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: After 10 years in the police force, a corporal never imagined that a routine anti-drug operation would turn life-threatening when a suspect armed with a parang slashed his left arm.
He said he was part of a police team that raided a house in Kampung Lalang Pepuyu, Tanah Merah, on Oct 17 as part of a special operation to curb drug abuse.
"The suspect and his mother were at the house when we arrived.
"The suspect was in a room when he spotted us entering his house. Armed with a parang, he immediately fled and ran towards the main road."
The corporal said he and his colleagues chased the suspect for about 1km before the man turned on him.
"We approached him, believing he was about to surrender.
"I went close to disarm him and take the parang from his hand.
"Instead, he swung the parang at me and slashed my left arm," said the 37-year-old when met today.
The father of three said the suspect was shirtless and wearing only shorts when the attack happened.
"I felt numbness in my left arm after being slashed. Then I saw blood coming out," he said.
The corporal said it was the first time in his decade-long career that he had faced a life-threatening situation while on duty.
"I am now stable and have been
discharged from hospital
, but I still need follow-up treatment," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Prisoner charged with murdering fellow inmate at Marang prison
Article:
MARANG: A prisoner was charged at the magistrate's court with the murder of another inmate at Marang Prison in August.
Che Mohd Nazzaruddin Che Ros, 35, is accused of killing Nor Mohd Helmi Sahari in Zone 2, R10, Marang Prison, between 8.45 am and 9.15 am on Aug 24.
The charge is framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or a maximum of 40 years' imprisonment and, where the death penalty is not imposed, not less than 12 strokes of the cane for male offenders under 50.
The accused was also not allowed bail. Deputy public prosecutor Noradila Ab Latif appeared for the prosecution, while Che Mohd Nazzaruddin was unrepresented.
Meanwhile, two other prisoners, Mohd Fadli Che Mansor, 36, and Nor Dhitauddin Afiq Norwadi, 22, pleaded not guilty in the same court to a charge of abetting or intentionally causing injury to the same victim on the same date, time and at the same location.
They are charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same Code, which carries a maximum of one year's jail or an RM2,000 fine, or both, upon conviction.
Magistrate Athirah Hashim allowed both accused, who were represented by National Legal Aid Foundation counsel Shameer Haziq Shaharuddin, bail of RM2,000 each with one surety.
The court fixed Nov 5 for mention of Mohd Fadli's and Nor Dhitauddin's case, and Dec 10 for Che Mohd Nazzaruddin's case.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Halal concerns prompt Jakim probe into chicken slaughtering
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) is investigating chicken slaughtering methods at a premises near Pudu Market following a video circulating on social media.
Its director-general Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee said in a statement that the probe also involved local authorities.
"A thorough investigation is being carried out into the issue involving a company that does not hold a Malaysia Halal Certification Certificate and the chicken issue currently circulating online," he said.
Putrajaya member of parliament Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin had urged Jakim to investigate the slaughtering methods, halal status and where the chicken processed at the premises was supplied and sold.
He also called for a joint investigation involving Kuala Lumpur City Hall, the Health Ministry and the Immigration Department to examine hygiene, compliance with the law, possible misuse of the halal logo and the work permit status of foreign workers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DNB, MRT Corp team up for 5G coverage at RTS immigration, customs complex
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) and MRT Corp have partnered to provide indoor 5G connectivity at the Rapid Transit System's (RTS) Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security complex (ICQC) in Johor Bahru.
The collaboration aims to provide comprehensive indoor 5G coverage across the RTS' ICQC complex, allowing commuters to access reliable connectivity and digital services, including ticketing, navigation, communications and mobile transactions.
The partnership was formalised through a memorandum of understanding exchanged between DNB chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail and MRT Corp chief executive officer Datuk Mohd Zarif Hashim at Transport Expo Asia 2026 today.
Azman said the RTS Link complex offered an opportunity to demonstrate the benefits of seamless indoor 5G connectivity and improve the commuter experience.
"Together with MRT Corp and our mobile network operator shareholders, we look forward to delivering a better commuter experience while creating a model for broader indoor 5G adoption across transport hubs, commercial developments and public venues nationwide," he said.
Zarif said the focus was shifting toward preparing the RTS Link for passenger operations, with reliable digital connectivity forming an important part of the overall travel experience.
He said the partnership allows MRT Corp to better utilise its infrastructure while enabling passengers to remain connected as they move through the station and immigration facilities.
Through its unit Malaysia Rapid Transit System Sdn Bhd, MRT Corp is responsible for developing and owning the Malaysian infrastructure for the RTS, including the in-building telecommunications infrastructure at the Bukit Chagar ICQS complex.
MRT Corp, which is a licensed network facilities provider under the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, intends to commercialise these facilities by leasing infrastructure and telecommunications space to mobile network operators.
The strategy forms part of its efforts to generate sustainable non-fare revenue and maximise the long-term value of its infrastructure investments.

Title: 20th AMMTC: Asean needs concrete actions to eradicate transnational crimes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks.
He said the threat of transnational crime has become increasingly complex due to the misuse of digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), necessitating a faster and more integrated response from Asean member states.
"Asean's success cannot be measured solely by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the criminal networks dismantled, the victims protected, and the criminals brought to justice.
"This is the commitment that Malaysia is bringing to Manila. Regional cooperation must yield tangible benefits for the security of the people, rather than remaining merely as commitments on paper," he said when delivering the National Statement at the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime (AMMTC) in Manila, Philippines, today.
Saifuddin Nasution said Malaysia has outlined three priorities to strengthen Asean cooperation: accelerating cross-border responses to online fraud and illicit financial flows; enhancing investigative capabilities including the handling of digital evidence and asset recovery; and improving operational collaboration between member states and international partners.
He said the need to expedite such cooperation has become increasingly urgent, given that proceeds of crime can be moved across borders in a matter of minutes, whereas investigative and legal processes typically take much longer.
Consequently, he argued that regional cooperation mechanisms must prioritise the detection of illicit funds, the preservation of digital evidence, and the coordination of investigations to ensure that criminal syndicates cannot exploit gaps in law enforcement between nations.
Saifuddin Nasution highlighted that as Malaysia prepares to chair Asean in 2025, the country has laid a crucial foundation for regional security cooperation through the adoption of the Asean Plan of Action to Combat Transnational Crime (2026–2035) and the Melaka Declaration.
He said the continuity of these efforts is further reinforced by the Work Programme of the Asean Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC) for 2026–2028, which was adopted last June.
"Currently, our primary challenge is to ensure that all frameworks for cooperation has resulted in tangible actions and outcomes," he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said Malaysia will continue to play an active role as an Asean voluntary lead country in the areas of money laundering and human trafficking, with the aim of strengthening information exchange, capacity building, and enforcement cooperation among member states.
He said Malaysia also hosted the inaugural meeting of the Asean Working Group on Money Laundering in Kuala Lumpur last April, as part of efforts to enhance the coordination of regional actions.
Saifuddin Nasution also shared the measures implemented by Malaysia to address transnational crime, including the establishment of the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) which operates 24 hours a day and can be reached via the 997 hotline since March.
He said Malaysia has strengthened its cyber-legal framework through the passing of the Cybercrime Bill 2026 in July, and has enhanced border controls by empowering the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency.
He added that efforts to combat terrorism and violent extremism are also being pursued through the Malaysia Action Plan on Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (MyPCVE) 2024–2028, which focuses on prevention, enforcement, rehabilitation, and reintegration.

Title: SC extends deadline for Yinson privatisation intention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) has approved an extension until Nov 30, 2026, for Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd (YLSB), MISC Bhd and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) to announce their intention regarding the proposed privatisation of Yinson Holdings Bhd.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing, Yinson Holdings said the SC announced this in its letter dated Oct 19, 2026. The extension will allow the parties to continue evaluating and discussing the proposed scheme.
"The proposed scheme remains subject to, amongst others, evaluations and negotiations among the parties, execution of definitive agreements, determination of the final offer price, and such other requisite approvals and conditions as may be determined.
"Accordingly, there can be no assurance that the discussions will lead to or result in the implementation of the proposed scheme," it said.
In a separate filing issued by MISC Bhd, the company said that the proposed privatisation of the offeree would be undertaken by way of a scheme of arrangement under Section 366 of the Companies Act 2016.
It also noted that this announcement does not constitute a firm intention to privatise the offeree (Yinson Holdings) and there is no certainty that any offer or transaction will ultimately be made.
On Aug 28, YLSB proposed a potential privatisation at an indicative offer price of RM2.35 per share following preliminary discussions with MISC, EPF, its affiliates, and other stakeholders.

Title: Thai court overturns attempted rape conviction of Olympic boxing champion
Article:
BANGKOK: A Thai appeals court overturned on Tuesday a conviction for the attempted rape of a teenage girl handed to the country's first Olympic gold medallist, but upheld his sentence for abduction.
Somluck Kamsing, now 53, became a national hero in Thailand when he won featherweight boxing gold at the 1996 Olympics in Atlanta.
He was found guilty in January 2025 of abduction for indecent purposes and attempted rape of a person aged between 15 and 18, and sentenced to just over three years in prison.
A regional appeals court in Khon Kaen dismissed the attempted rape conviction on Tuesday, saying the victim's testimony contained "inconsistencies" and there was no evidence of coercion or threats.
Somluck's sentence was adjusted to two years, the court said in a media statement.
A 17-year-old girl filed a complaint against Somluck in December 2023, saying he had assaulted her in a hotel in Khon Kaen, a city in Thailand's northeast.
The court said on Tuesday the pair met in a bar and she went back to his hotel on his motorcycle.
Somluck, who also won boxing titles at the 1994 and 1998 Asian Games in Hiroshima and Bangkok respectively, denied the allegations.--AFP

Title: Gamuda, Perak state govt ink deal to implement Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd today announced that an agreement to implement the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme (NPWSS) has been signed between the State Government of Perak, Khazanah Air Perak Sdn Bhd (KAP), and Prasarana Air dan Irigasi Perak Sdn Bhd (PAIPP).
KAP is a 50:50 joint venture company between Gamuda and Perbadanan Kemajuan Negeri Perak (PKNPk), while PAIPP is KAP's wholly owned subsidiary.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Gamuda said that under the NPWSS agreement, the state government will appoint KAP and PAIPP to develop, operate and maintain the NPWSS, with PAIPP responsible for the WTP scope and KAP responsible for the source works scope.
"The NPWSS agreement formalises PAIPP's appointment as the WTP operator to undertake the water treatment plant (WTP) Scope, including the right to abstract raw water for the Phase 1 WTP, and KAP's role in the source works scope," it said.
The NPWSS is a national project and a strategic initiative by the state and federal governments to mitigate long-standing water shortages for irrigation, domestic and industrial use in the northern region of Perak.
The NPWSS is designed to transfer up to 1,500 million litres per day (MLD) of raw water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah Dam, with 500 MLD designated for Northern Perak's immediate irrigation needs.
The balance of 1,000 MLD is intended to meet Perak's domestic and industrial water demands, including supplying treated water to Phase 2 of the Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park (KIGIP), with any surplus for sale as treated water to Perbadanan Bekalan Air Pulau Pinang Sdn Bhd (PBAPP).

Title: RedPlanet's adjusted FY26 profit jumps 35pct ahead of listing
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RedPlanet Bhd's adjusted net profit rose 35.1 per cent to RM7.31 million for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), ahead of its transfer from Bursa Malaysia's LEAP Market to the ACE Market on Oct 22.
The enterprise information and communications technology (ICT) solutions provider recorded revenue of RM40.72 million, up 22.3 per cent from RM33.3 million a year earlier.
Its adjusted net profit excludes RM980,000 in non-recurring expenses related to its initial public offering (IPO) and listing.
On a reported basis, RedPlanet's profit increased 21.3 per cent to RM6.33 million from RM5.22 million previously.
Geospatial solutions remained the largest revenue contributor at RM18.4 million, accounting for 45.1 per cent of total revenue.
Intelligent rail solutions contributed RM11.6 million, or 28.4 per cent, while ICT trading and ancillary hardware generated RM10.8 million.
Malaysia accounted for 87 per cent of revenue, with the remainder coming from overseas markets.
For the fourth quarter, RedPlanet posted revenue of RM7.55 million and net profit of RM1.36 million. Excluding listing-related expenses, quarterly net profit stood at RM1.57 million.
Its financial position remained healthy, with cash, bank balances and fixed deposits of RM13.8 million against borrowings of RM5.2 million as at June 30.
Operating cash flow more than doubled to RM9.5 million from RM4.7 million a year earlier.
RedPlanet's IPO comprises 70 million new shares priced at 19 sen each, raising RM13.3 million, alongside an offer for sale of 10 million existing shares.
Its public share allocation was oversubscribed 85.28 times.
The company expects to benefit from growth in Malaysia's geospatial and intelligent rail solutions industries.

Title: Iran prolongs talks in stalemate to influence US midterms, officials say
Article:
DUBAI: Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the US to try to weaken Donald Trump politically ahead of November's US midterm elections, senior officials say, while fears of renewed military action and deep distrust of Washington have reinforced Teheran's reluctance to strike a quick deal to end the war.
Three senior Iranian officials and an Iranian insider, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Teheran was convinced the US president was ready to resort to renewed attacks to try to break the stalemate in the eight-month-old war.
"Iran is preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal with America to end the war," one of the officials said. "The clerical establishment is determined not to give Trump a political victory."
Teheran analyst Saeed Leylaz said that, by prolonging the talks, "Iran is influencing the US election without taking any unlawful action."
The war, which began in February when the US and its ally Israel launched strikes on Iran, has helped drive Trump's approval rating to a record low as polls suggest that Americans worried about high gasoline prices will punish his Republican Party in the Nov 3 congressional elections.
Trump has repeatedly said he expects oil prices to drop after the elections, but has not offered a detailed plan to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route effectively closed by Iran since the war began.
Iranian attacks both threatened and real have kept ship traffic through the strait to a trickle, while a US maritime blockade and trade sanctions have cut off Iran's oil export revenues and exacerbated growing domestic economic woes.
With Teheran refusing to make concessions it believes could benefit Trump politically, there is little chance of a breakthrough before the elections, the officials said.
Under pressure from Israel, Washington wants Iran's decades-long nuclear programme - which Iran says is purely peaceful and Western powers allege has military dimensions - on the table from the outset.
For its part, Teheran insists that its conditions under a "seven-day plan" must be met before nuclear negotiations begin. And it offers no prospect of giving up the leverage over the Strait of Hormuz that the conflict prompted it to seize.
Iran's Foreign Ministry and the US White House did not respond to Reuters requests for comment.
Iran's proposal, conveyed through Qatari mediators, offered to reopen the strait within seven days, albeit under Iranian control, provided that Washington lifted its maritime blockade, eased restrictions on Iranian oil exports, released frozen assets and ended hostilities on all fronts.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the offer remained on the table, with messages being exchanged through mediators.
Teheran's view that Washington cannot be trusted to commit to diplomacy stems from the attacks on Iran that have derailed previous negotiations, one Iranian official said.
In June 2025, an Israeli attack wrecked plans for a sixth round of US-Iran nuclear talks in Oman. And last February, the US and Israel launched their war just after another round of talks ended, with further technical discussions scheduled.
Maintaining a state somewhere between war and peace through the US midterms allows Iran to sustain pressure on Washington while reiterating its commitment to diplomacy.
Trump has said the US will not bomb Iran again before Nov 3.
However, the officials said Teheran continues to expect that bombing will resume, sooner or later.
Alex Vatanka, director of the Iran program at the Middle East Institute in Washington, said the clerical establishment clearly wanted to hurt Trump politically.
"But the fundamental issue is that Teheran believes that Trump is interested in regime change ... and following Israeli Prime Minister (Benjamin) Netanyahu's policy of seeking to bring down Iran's ruling establishment," he said.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed Iran with Netanyahu on Monday, three Israeli officials said, in an unannounced visit to Israel a week before a parliamentary election in which Netanyahu's position is at risk.
Iran's strategy of keeping negotiations alive without rushing towards agreement comes at a cost.
Prolonged uncertainty is weighing on Iran's already crippled economy and wearing down public patience. Thousands were killed at the turn of the year when the security forces crushed spiralling anti-government protests.
Annual inflation hit 73.6 per cent in September, according to the Statistical Centre of Iran, and the rial currency has fallen nearly 35 per cent against the dollar since Washington reapplied its naval blockade in July.
Iran's seaborne crude exports fell to zero in the second week of September from a 14-day average of 230,000 barrels per day at the start of the month, and remained there as of Oct 5, according to energy intelligence platform Vortexa.
But the leadership's distrust of Washington extends beyond the current conflict to existential concerns.
Iran believes the US has repeatedly broken agreements even when Teheran honoured its commitments, Leylaz said, leaving little confidence that any comprehensive deal would endure.
"Reaching a sustainable deal with the US, even after the Trump administration, is no longer possible because of the deepened distrust," Leylaz said. "Nothing will go back to the pre-war status quo."

Title: Selangor Sultan warns royal family against abusing status
Article:
KLANG: Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain.
His Royal Highness stressed that royal status did not give anyone the right to act as they pleased, reminding family members to respect the law and comply with all regulations.
"We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. Every family member is accountable for their conduct and actions, as the behaviour of one individual can affect public perceptions of the entire royal family.
"The way we conduct ourselves, interact with society and fulfil our responsibilities must reflect the dignity and integrity of the royal family and institution," His Royal Highness said at a royal tea reception with members of the royal family in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of his reign at Padang Mahkota, Istana Alam Shah, here today.
Also present were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah and his wife, Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz.
The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.
His Royal Highness said differences of opinion and misunderstandings should be resolved wisely and amicably, without spreading false stories, provoking disputes or making hurtful remarks.
"Be mindful of your words and manners, including when using social media, and practise mutual understanding, tolerance and forgiveness.
"I also urge family members to support and care for one another. We should not gather only for ceremonies and celebrations but also offer help and support when our relatives face difficulties," the Sultan said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also called for compassion, responsibility and mutual respect between older and younger generations to be nurtured and passed down to future generations.
The Sultan also expressed delight at the attendance of nearly 1,200 members of the Selangor royal family, saying the Silver Jubilee celebration provided a meaningful opportunity to strengthen family ties.
"Some of my relatives who are here this afternoon are people I have not seen for a long time, while others belong to the younger generation who have now reached adulthood. Your presence means a great deal to me.
"This gathering not only brings me joy but also reminds us of our shared responsibility to preserve family harmony and the dignity of the Selangor royal institution," His Royal Highness said. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One in three Americans back second execution attempt after failed one, poll finds
Article:
WASHINGTON: One-third of Americans think the government should try a second time to put a convicted criminal to death if a first execution attempt fails, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted after a botched lethal injection in Tennessee.
The four-day poll, completed on Monday, showed 39 per cent of respondents thought the government should instead allow convicts to serve life in prison following a failed execution, while 26 per cent were not sure which was a better approach.
The nationwide survey found minority public support for trying again to execute inmates who survive execution attempts, a question Tennessee now faces after Christa Pike, 50, survived two lethal injection attempts last month in Nashville.
The convicted murderer was taken to a hospital unconscious following the attempted execution, critically ill and with severe arm injuries after two syringes of the caustic barbiturate pentobarbital failed to kill her, marking Tennessee's second botched lethal injection this year.
She did not regain consciousness until five days later.
Most countries around the world, along with 23 US states, have abolished capital punishment.
Those US states that still impose it have struggled in recent years to obtain execution drugs, and some have considered other methods, including firing squads.
A slight majority of Americans — 55 per cent — continue to support capital punishment for people convicted of the most serious crimes, down from 63 per cent who said in a 2017 Reuters/Ipsos poll that they supported the policy.
Some 31 per cent of respondents in the latest poll said they opposed the death penalty, while 13 per cent either did not know or did not answer the question.
The issue has taken on new significance as courts consider whether states can make a second execution attempt after a failed one.
[[nid:1559906]]
The US Supreme Court recently allowed a state to proceed with scheduling a second execution date after a failed attempt.
Kenneth Smith, convicted of a 1988 murder-for-hire, survived a trip to Alabama's execution chamber in 2022 after prison officials failed to set up intravenous lines.
But Alabama succeeded on its second try in 2024 with a new method of suffocation using nitrogen gas.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth recently floated the prospect of the first-ever livestream of a US execution, the planned death by firing squad of Nidal Hasan, the former US Army major who killed 13 people at Texas' Fort Hood military base.
Following widespread criticism – including from Republican lawmakers – President Donald Trump cancelled the livestream plans, though officials still intend to carry out the execution on Dec 3.
Some 46 per cent of Americans, including 29 per cent of Democrats and 71 per cent of Republicans, said it was appropriate to execute Hasan by firing squad.
But 71 per cent of people surveyed, including majorities of Democrats and Republicans, said showing executions to the public on television or the internet was inappropriate.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll was conducted online and nationwide, gathering responses from 1,679 US adults. It had a margin of error of two percentage points.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 3 ministries will decide on school closures as haze persists, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Any decision to close schools amid the ongoing haze will be made jointly by the Education Ministry (MOE), Health Ministry (MOH) and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on their respective expertise, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said the decision would be based on air quality monitoring and health considerations to ensure students' safety, while also considering the impact on learning loss if schools were closed for too long.
"From time to time, these three ministries will sit down and make a decision based on the expertise available, particularly at the MOH and NRES levels.
"We hope this will not be prolonged because we know the impact if school closures continue. So it requires a very careful approach and guidance before we make a decision," she told reporters after the Anti-Bullying Literacy programme marking the Anti-Bullying Act 2026, held with the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department at the Teacher Education Institute (IPG), Bahasa Melayu Campus, today.
Also present was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
