Title: Bank Negara unveils tokenised bonds platform
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has launched a new platform to facilitate the issuance, depository and safekeeping of tokenised bonds and sukuk.
Known as Ssds+, the platform is designed to streamline transactions, provide greater flexibility in structuring financial instruments and expand access to investment opportunities.
Bank Negara said the platform was developed in-house using cloud and distributed ledger technologies.
It builds on the existing scripless securities depository system, which serves as the central securities depository for the wholesale financial market.
Beyond wholesale issuances, Ssds+ is also equipped to support tokenised government and retail bonds, with its integration with Rentas+ enabling secure payment and settlement services around the clock.
The platform manages the transfer of tokenised securities and maintains ownership records, while Rentas+ facilitates the corresponding payments for bond purchases in central bank money.
Bank Negara governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the launch marks a major milestone in modernising Malaysia's financial market infrastructure.
He said Ssds+ and Rentas+ will provide a secure, faster, more flexible and digitally enabled foundation for new applications in securities and payments.
"These platforms will support innovation and contribute to more efficient and responsive financial markets," he said in a statement today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Schools remain open in six states, KL and Putrajaya tomorrow, outdoor activities halted
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak, Pahang and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, will operate as usual tomorrow, with outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In NEGERI SEMBILAN, the state Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) would operate as usual. However, the Final Academic Session Exam (UASA) scheduled during this period must be postponed and rescheduled by the respective schools.
The postponement also applies to all internal school examinations, in line with the MOE’s statement dated October 15. All outdoor activities must be suspended if the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 100.
In MELAKA, SELANGOR, PUTRAJAYA and KUALA LUMPUR, school administrators were instructed to monitor API readings issued by the Department of Environment and pay particular attention to pupils at higher risk.
In PAHANG, the state Education Department said schools in Rompin, Bentong and Cameron Highlands would operate tomorrow, but all outdoor activities would be suspended.
Schools in other districts would operate as usual, with any changes to be announced through the respective District Education Offices.
The PERAK Education Department urged everyone to remain alert to developments and heed the authorities’ advice on the haze.
In PENANG, the state Education Department encouraged pupils to drink sufficient water and instructed schools to ensure an adequate supply of drinking water.
Pupils and school staff are also encouraged to wear face masks as a precaution, particularly those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups.
The education departments in Melaka, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Perak and Penang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, have also given parents and guardians who are concerned about their children’s health the option of keeping them at home, provided they inform the school.
Earlier, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said that decisions on school closures due to the haze were made jointly by the MOE, the Health Ministry (MOH) and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on the expertise of each ministry.
She said the decisions took into account air quality monitoring and the health risks to pupils, as well as the impact on learning if schools remained closed for too long.
Meanwhile, Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia has urged the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive, collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families.
Her Majesty stressed the importance of community cooperation to strengthen the effectiveness of home-based teaching and learning (PdPR), as well as developing long-term strategies to deal with the haze. — Bernama

Title: From Waze to TuJu? Anwar backs Malaysian navigation app over data security concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is encouraging the public to use the locally developed application, TuJu created by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) as an alternative for road navigation needs.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this alternative has been proposed due to security risks concerning information and data on citizens’ movements, given that the Waze application is subject to the laws of the Israeli government.
He noted that this matter was among the topics discussed while chairing the third meeting of the National Cyber Security Committee (JKSN) today, which aimed to examine evolving cyber threats and strengthen the nation’s preparedness and digital sovereignty.
“Also discussed were the implementation of the Cyber Security Act 2024, the security of MyDigital ID, preparations to counter threats from quantum computing through post-quantum cryptography (PQC), emerging threats involving autonomous artificial intelligence, and the protection of National Critical Information Infrastructure (NCII).
“We cannot compromise when it comes to the security of our citizens’ data and identities. Therefore, the government is strengthening an integrated identity ecosystem utilising MyKad as a physical credential and MyDigital ID for digital transactions supported by more robust cyber protections, including preparations for future threats via PQC,” he said in a Facebook post.
The prime minister emphasised that these efforts are crucial to ensuring that the digitalization of public services continues to benefit the people, without compromising security, public trust, or national sovereignty. — Bernama

Title: No action against UM student over viral ‘tough’ question, says Zambry
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) and Universiti Malaya (UM) have no intention of taking action against the student who went viral recently after asking a “tough” question during the i-Future programme.
Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the ministry maintained its position that students’ right to freedom of expression must be respected, while condemning any form of abuse, insults or threats directed at the student on social media.
“My position is clear. Respect students’ right to speak up. As we have stated, amendments to the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) have provided them with the space to express their views.
“This freedom should also be exercised responsibly, courteously and based on facts,” he said in a statement shared on TikTok today.
Earlier, a video lasting more than two minutes went viral, showing a Universiti Malaya Students’ Union representative firmly questioning a panel during a dialogue session held as part of the i-Future programme.
The student, among other things, expressed concerns about the integrity of leadership and criticised the collection of public donations to help former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak pay the RM50 million fine imposed as one of the conditions for allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence for the SRC International case under house arrest.
Commenting on allegations of threats, abuse and condemnation directed at the student, Zambry said such behaviour should not occur and advised the student to lodge a police report to enable an investigation.
He urged the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission to examine the posts and accounts involved, including the possibility that fake accounts had been used.
“If anyone has attempted to engage in wrongdoing, the student concerned should take appropriate action by lodging a report with the relevant authorities,” he said.
Zambry urged all parties not to politicise the issue or exploit students to advance specific agendas.
“I also urge everyone not to turn students into weapons of political propaganda, to the extent that they become victims of certain agendas.
“For example, some ministers have even called for shirts, T-shirts and the like to be made, whereas at the MOHE level, we have absolutely no intention of taking any action against the student concerned,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No driving licences without tests: JPJ warns against fake TikTok promotions
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) has denied the authenticity of a TikTok advertisement offering driving licences without the need to take a test.
In a statement today, JPJ said it received complaints regarding the advertisement, which used an account under the name ‘Ahmad Mushidi’.
“JPJ wishes to emphasise that the advertisement and the account belonging to the individual named Ahmad Mushidi are fake,” the statement read.
Following this, JPJ lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for further action.
JPJ advised the public not to be easily deceived by driving licence promotions through unverified advertisements or accounts to avoid confusion and losses.
The public is also reminded to obtain information regarding JPJ services only through the department’s official platforms. — Bernama

Title: Kampar woman loses over RM129,000 in online job scam
Article:
IPOH, Oct 20 — A local woman suffered losses of more than RM129,000 after being duped by a non-existent online part-time job offer.
Kampar District Police Chief Supt Mohamad Nazri Daud said that his department received a report yesterday from the 34-year-old victim.
“Initial police investigations found that the victim saw an offer for a part-time job related to hotel bookings through social media. Interested, the victim left her phone number to be contacted by the party offering the job.
“The victim received a message from an unknown individual offering the job. The victim was then added to a WhatsApp group supposedly for handling online hotel booking transactions,” he said in a statement today.
Mohamad Nazri said the victim was instructed to make payments for each hotel booking into several bank accounts provided by the suspect, who promised that the capital would be returned along with a commission ranging between 10 to 20 percent, which would increase according to the transaction amount.
He said that due to being lured by the offer and the promise of profits, the victim carried out several money transfer transactions to eight accounts provided by the suspect.
“The victim began to realise she had been cheated when the promised capital and commission were not received after the payments were made. The victim suffered a loss of RM129,975.54,” he said.
He added that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis record highest drug abuse rates
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis recorded the highest rates of drug or substance addiction and abuse in the country, based on statistics up to June 2026, said National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh.
He said Terengganu recorded the highest rate at 735 individuals per 100,000 population, followed by Kelantan (694), Kedah (669) and Perlis (646).
“The ranking of these four states reflects the extent of drug addiction and abuse that requires attention and targeted intervention.
“Geographical factors also contribute to this situation, with cross-border smuggling routes identified as among the risk factors influencing drug-related problems in these areas,” he said in a statement today.
Ruslin said a total of 130,307 drug and substance abuse cases were recorded nationwide during the same period, equivalent to a rate of 381 individuals per 100,000 population.
He said the statistics were compiled based on integrated data from four main sources, namely Nada, the Royal Malaysia Police, the Health Ministry and private rehabilitation centres.
In this regard, Ruslin said Nada was focusing on enforcement, prevention programmes and community empowerment in high-risk states, targeting three main segments: educational institutions, families and communities.
“A total of 242 prevention and public awareness programmes were conducted, involving 16,408 participants overall, including 228 programmes in Terengganu, Kelantan and Kedah, which involved more than 16,000 participants,” he said.
He added that 4,253 enforcement operations had been conducted nationwide, with 30,157 individuals detained for treatment and rehabilitation programmes as of last Sunday.
On treatment and rehabilitation, Ruslin said Nada prioritised a voluntary approach, with the average number of individuals seeking treatment on their own initiative rising from 75 a month in 2025 to 232 a month this year.
“This increase reflects positive progress following the implementation of amendments to the Drug Dependants (Treatment and Rehabilitation) Act 1983, which came into force on Aug 22, 2025,” he said.
He said Nada would continue to adopt a data-driven approach and strengthen cooperation with state governments through the Drug Eradication Action Council (MTMD) meetings to coordinate prevention, treatment and rehabilitation efforts involving various agencies, families, educational institutions and communities.

Title: Selangor Education Department cooperating with probe into schoolgirl’s death
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 20 — The Selangor State Education Department (JPN Selangor) will fully cooperate with the authorities’ investigations into the death of a Year One pupil after she experienced breathing difficulties at a school in Sepang.
In a statement today, JPN Selangor said the girl was reported to have had breathing difficulties at school and was taken to hospital for treatment.
“JPN Selangor extends its condolences and deepest sympathies to the pupil’s family. The department will ensure that the family’s welfare is given due attention, including assistance and psychosocial support as needed,” it said.
JPN Selangor will also ensure that due attention is given to the welfare and wellbeing of the school community affected by the incident.
“The public is advised not to speculate or spread unverified information regarding the incident. All parties are urged to respect the family’s privacy and give the authorities room to carry out their investigation,” the statement read.
Earlier, police confirmed that a seven-year-old girl died after she was believed to have experienced breathing difficulties while in class in Dengkil yesterday.
Sepang police chief ACP Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report on the incident at 7.30 pm yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Police record statements over podcast video on alleged drug trafficking
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Police have opened an investigation into the circulation of a podcast video alleging that drug trafficking activities were taking place at a house of worship near the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here.
Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the investigation was being conducted under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
He said the investigation was initiated following a police report lodged by the chairman of the Marathadi Madurai Veeran Temple in Kuala Lumpur last Sunday to strongly deny the allegations made in the video.
“After receiving the Order to Investigate (OTI) from the Deputy Public Prosecutor, police have called several witnesses to assist in completing the investigation,” he said in a statement today.
He said the podcast guest, Azrul Affandi Sobry, will appear at the Sentul IPD at noon tomorrow to have his statement recorded.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus was previously reported as saying that the allegations raised in the video posted on the @Sembangohhyeahh TikTok account actually referred to an incident that occurred 10 years ago.
He said checks found that the incident took place on July 12, 2016, and that the podcast content was merely a retelling of the guest’s experience while monitoring the situation as a journalist at the time.
Fadil also stressed that such publicity was inappropriate as it could create negative public perceptions of the level of integrity of police, and advised all parties to be more responsible when disseminating information. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution urges Asean to translate anti-crime pledges into results
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — Asean must ensure that all commitments and cooperation frameworks agreed upon to combat transnational crime are translated into concrete action specifically in addressing online fraud, money laundering, and human smuggling.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the success of regional security cooperation should not be measured by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the effectiveness of enforcement actions taken against criminal networks.
He noted that the threat of transnational crime has become increasingly complex due to the misuse of digital technology and artificial intelligence (AI), necessitating a faster and more integrated response from Asean member states.
"Asean’s success cannot be measured solely by the number of agreements reached, but rather by the criminal networks dismantled, the victims protected, and the criminals brought to justice.
"This is the commitment that Malaysia is bringing to Manila. Regional cooperation must yield tangible benefits for the security of the people, rather than remaining merely as commitments on paper," he said when delivering the National Statement at the 20th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Transnational Crime (AMMTC) in Manila, Philippines, today.
Saifuddin Nasution noted that Malaysia has outlined three priorities to strengthen Asean cooperation: accelerating cross-border responses to online fraud and illicit financial flows; enhancing investigative capabilities including the handling of digital evidence and asset recovery; and improving operational collaboration between member states and international partners.
He emphasised that the need to expedite such cooperation has become increasingly urgent, given that proceeds of crime can be moved across borders in a matter of minutes, whereas investigative and legal processes typically take much longer.
Consequently, he argued that regional cooperation mechanisms must prioritise the detection of illicit funds, the preservation of digital evidence, and the coordination of investigations to ensure that criminal syndicates cannot exploit gaps in law enforcement between nations.
Saifuddin Nasution highlighted that as Malaysia prepares to chair Asean in 2025, the country has laid a crucial foundation for regional security cooperation through the adoption of the Asean Plan of Action to Combat Transnational Crime (2026-2035) and the Melaka Declaration.
He added that the continuity of these efforts is further reinforced by the Work Programme of the Asean Senior Officials Meeting on Transnational Crime (SOMTC) for 2026-2028, which was adopted last June.
"Currently, our primary challenge is to ensure that all frameworks for cooperation has resulted in tangible actions and outcomes," he said.
Meanwhile, Saifuddin Nasution said Malaysia will continue to play an active role as an Asean voluntary lead country in the areas of money laundering and human trafficking, with the aim of strengthening information exchange, capacity building, and enforcement cooperation among member states.
He noted that Malaysia also hosted the inaugural meeting of the Asean Working Group on Money Laundering in Kuala Lumpur last April, as part of efforts to enhance the coordination of regional actions.
Saifuddin Nasution also shared the measures implemented by Malaysia to address transnational crime, including the establishment of the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) which operates 24 hours a day and can be reached via the 997 hotline since March.
Furthermore, he mentioned that Malaysia has strengthened its cyber-legal framework through the passing of the Cybercrime Bill 2026 in July, and has enhanced border controls by empowering the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency.
He added that efforts to combat terrorism and violent extremism are also being pursued through the Malaysia Action Plan on Preventing and Countering Violent Extremism (MyPCVE) 2024-2028, which focuses on prevention, enforcement, rehabilitation, and reintegration. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi calls for stronger Asean cooperation on child online safety
Article:
BALI, Oct 20 — Asean countries must work together to protect children from growing online threats despite differences in their laws and approaches to internet safety, said Malaysia’s Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said countries in the region shared the challenge of keeping the internet safe for children and needed to strengthen cooperation to address these threats.
“The internet is good. The internet can be put to good use. But do children know how to use it well?” he said in his keynote address at Bali Tech Week 2026, initiated by Indonesia’s Ministry of Communication and Digital today.
Fahmi said Malaysia wanted to ensure that children below the age of 16 were unable to open social media accounts, although approaches to online safety for children could differ between Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore and other Asean countries.
Malaysia began enforcing age-verification requirements for social media account registration on June 1 this year under the Child Protection Code and Risk Mitigation Code introduced under the Online Safety Act 2025.
Under the new regulations, individuals under the age of 16 are no longer allowed to open any social media accounts, while those who wish to register must submit official identification documents such as MyKad, passport or MyDigital ID to verify their age.
Fahmi also highlighted the challenges posed by social media algorithms, noting that governments had limited understanding of how they operated and influenced the content users encountered.
At the forum, Fahmi outlined Malaysia’s efforts to improve internet coverage, speed and affordability while making online access safer, particularly for children.
Highlighting the dangers children faced online, he cited a recent case in which Malaysian police apprehended 53 suspected paedophiles and seized more than half a million files suspected of containing child sexual abuse material.
He described online child protection as a challenge faced by countries across the region.
Fahmi also said that governments needed to consider how they shaped people’s choices while ensuring individuals had the freedom to make more informed decisions.
Bali Tech Week, themed “Archipelago Ascending: Advance Together, Innovate Further”, is being held from Oct 19 to 23 at the Bali Beach Convention Centre in Sanur, bringing together policymakers, technology leaders, innovators and investors.
Fahmi was invited by his Indonesian counterpart, Meutya Hafid, to deliver the keynote address at the event during his working visit to Indonesia from Monday to Thursday.
He will travel to Jakarta later Tuesday to continue his official engagements. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin saddened by Perikatan deregistration, warns against abuse of power in coalitions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin today expressed sadness over the deregistration of Perikatan Nasional (PN), describing the development as a lesson for leaders of political coalitions to act fairly towards all member parties and comply with their constitutions and the law.
In a statement, Muhyiddin, who founded PN, said he was saddened by the coalition's deregistration.
"However, this decision is a reminder to any party leading a coalition to act fairly towards all member parties and to always comply with the party constitution and the Societies Act 1966," he said.
Muhyiddin also cautioned against the misuse of power and position within a political coalition for the benefit of a particular party or group.
He said such actions could cause a coalition to drift away from the original objectives and purpose behind its formation.
"Do not misuse power and position in a coalition solely for the interests of a particular party or group to the point where the coalition deviates from its original goals and objectives," he said.
Muhyiddin added that he would discuss the way forward with the Bersatu leadership at a special Political Bureau meeting scheduled for tonight.
Earlier today, the Registrar of Societies announced the deregistration of PN after finding that the coalition's explanation had failed to rebut the grounds for deregistration stated in an earlier notice.

Title: Selangor Sultan cautions royal family members against exploiting royal status
Article:
KLANG, Oct 20 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has warned members of the Selangor royal family against exploiting their royal status to deceive others for personal gain.
His Royal Highness stressed that royal status did not give anyone the right to act as they pleased, reminding family members to respect the law and comply with all regulations.
“We have a responsibility to protect the reputation of the Selangor royal family and institution. Every family member is accountable for their conduct and actions, as the behaviour of one individual can affect public perceptions of the entire royal family.
“The way we conduct ourselves, interact with society and fulfil our responsibilities must reflect the dignity and integrity of the royal family and institution,” His Royal Highness said at a royal tea reception with members of the royal family in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee of His Royal Highness’s reign at Padang Mahkota, Istana Alam Shah, here today.
Also present were Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah and his wife, Datin Paduka Seri Afzaa Fadini Abdul Aziz.
The Sultan also urged family members to maintain strong bonds, avoid hostility and prevent minor disagreements from causing divisions within the extended royal family.
His Royal Highness said differences of opinion and misunderstandings should be resolved wisely and amicably, without spreading false stories, provoking disputes or making hurtful remarks.
“Be mindful of your words and manners, including when using social media, and practise mutual understanding, tolerance and forgiveness.
“I also urge family members to support and care for one another. We should not gather only for ceremonies and celebrations but also offer help and support when our relatives face difficulties,” the Sultan said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also called for the values of compassion, responsibility and mutual respect between older and younger generations to be nurtured and passed down to future generations.
At the same time, the Sultan also expressed delight at the attendance of nearly 1,200 members of the Selangor royal family, saying the Silver Jubilee celebration provided a meaningful opportunity to strengthen family ties.
“Some of my relatives who are here this afternoon are people I have not seen for a long time, while others belong to the younger generation who have now reached adulthood. Your presence means a great deal to me.
“This gathering not only brings me joy but also reminds us of our shared responsibility to preserve family harmony and the dignity of the Selangor royal institution,” His Royal Highness said. — Bernama

Title: Anwar backs efforts to strengthen IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has welcomed efforts to strengthen the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, positioning it as a hub for the sharing of knowledge and expertise.
He noted that Malaysia is recognised for its experience in empowering micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs), strengthening economic resilience, and generating employment opportunities, expertise and experience that could potentially benefit other IsDB member countries.
“I also emphasised Malaysia’s readiness to share its expertise and expand development cooperation at the international level,” he said in a post on X today.
He mentioned that this was discussed during a meeting today with IsDB president Dr. Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser, reflecting a continued confidence in the nation’s development trajectory and governance.
“God willing, this close collaboration will further enhance Malaysia’s role as a credible development partner, while bringing the expertise of our people to the global stage,” he added.
The IsDB Centre of Excellence in Kuala Lumpur, launched in 2019, serves as a strategic platform for the transfer of technology, expertise, and best practices in Islamic finance from Malaysia to the 56 other IsDB member countries.
The IsDB, headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, is a multilateral development finance institution established in 1975 to support the economic development and social progress of its member countries and Muslim communities worldwide, based on Shariah principles. — Bernama

Title: Schools still first channel to seek justice for bullying, Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB) only next option, says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Students struggling with bullying should seek justice through their schools first before bringing their grievances to the Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB), said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Azalina said the TAB would also evaluate the complaints received before accepting the relevant cases for mediation to prevent it from being overwhelmed with the high volume of complaints.
She said the TAB serves as a deterrence measure, similar to the Anti-Sexual Harassment Tribunal (TAGS) established in March 2024, and would function as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism outside the schools and courts.
However, she also stressed that the TAB is not a substitute for the courts and that it would be impartial to both bullying victims and perpetrators.
“The tribunal looks at both the victim and the perpetrator. So, it is not just going to look at damages or compensations.
“When they issue an award, they will also add in certain assistance on emotional challenges, for example,” she said, after attending the Anti-Bullying Literacy Programme at IPG Kampus Bahasa Melayu, here today.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek was also present at the event.
According to Azalina, the TAB has clocked 68 cases since its launch in June, with adolescents in the secondary schools aged between 13 and 17 students forming the bulk of the cases (42 cases).
Majority of the reported cases were from Selangor and Kuala Lumpur (11 cases).
Azalina said the rising numbers of cases reflect growing awareness on bullying, which she said would eventually reduce bullying incidents as perpetrators would realise that the TAB will hold them accountable.
She said the Cabinet will also look into the possibility of extending the services of TAB to adults aged above 18 facing bullying.
However, she said the ministry would first deliberate the matter with the Higher Education Ministry and the Human Resources Ministry before moving forward.
Citing countries like New Zealand and the United Kingdom, Azalina said the government should consider providing trauma handling training, private counselling sessions and psychological intervention for teachers handling bullying cases.
“Teachers should not be left to struggle alone when handling trauma of students,” she said.
Established in June 2026, the TAB operates under the purview of the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department (BHEUU) and is led by experienced sessions court judges and magistrates.
The TAB can issue a variety of awards such as apologies, removal of digital content, reimbursement of expenses, compensation or damages or other relevant measures.

Title: Uphold Malay language without neglecting English, says Fadhlina
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 20 — The Malay language must be consistently upheld without neglecting English proficiency among the younger generation, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said efforts to strengthen the language should be pursued through various platforms, including public speaking competitions, which provide higher education students with opportunities to express their views through well-reasoned, knowledge-based arguments.
“The policy of upholding the Malay language while strengthening English proficiency is crucial to the country.
“We must remain consistent in ensuring that the use, enrichment and wider adoption of the Malay language remain part of the national agenda,” she said at the final of the Arena Wacana Aspirasi Mahasiswa oratory competition, held in conjunction with the 2026 National Language Decade (DBK), at Universiti Teknikal Malaysia Melaka (UTeM) in Durian Tunggal here today.
The competition was won by Putra Haikal Ikhwansyah Nafarulzian, a third-year Bachelor of Laws with Honours student at Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), who took home RM1,000 in prize money.
Second place went to Yang Asyraf Asyran Yang Rashidi, a final-year student pursuing a Bachelor of Chemical Engineering Technology (Industrial Chemical Process) at Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP), who received RM800.
Fadhlina said oratory competitions not only encouraged the continued use of the national language but also helped enrich vocabulary and improve language skills among the public.
She added that such competitions played an important role in fostering a culture of knowledge, particularly by teaching young people to express their views clearly, respectfully and in a well-structured manner, supported by sound arguments. — Bernama

Title: Families, seniors welcome ECRL fare discounts
Article:
KUANTAN, Oct 20 — A 50 per cent discount on East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) fares for eligible passengers positions the rail service as a new, more affordable transport option particularly for families traveling with children and senior citizens.
Civil servant Fairus Mohd, 42, noted that the discount allows her to bring along her three children-aged between three and seven as well as her 75-year-old mother, Jeriah Abdul Rahman, for a trip to Kuala Lumpur via the ECRL.
She mentioned that her family occasionally travels to the capital for various personal matters and to visit relatives.
“With this discount, I can better manage travel expenses especially when traveling with my children and elderly mother while also avoiding road congestion, particularly during festive seasons and school holidays,” she told Bernama.
According to Fairus, ECRL also offers her children a novel experience, allowing them to enjoy a train journey and take in the scenery along the route.
“In my view, the ticket price is reasonable, and the service is expected to offer comfort while shortening travel time. My family and I are looking forward to trying it out, and I hope there will be plenty of tickets available,” said the Pahang native.
She added that while air travel was previously a primary choice for those looking to reach their destinations quickly, the ECRL now provides an additional land-based transport alternative for travel between the East Coast and the Klang Valley.
For 60-year-old senior citizen Noril Azian Jaafar, the 50 per cent fare discount offered by the ECRL service is a highly beneficial initiative that helps save on travel costs, while also providing her with the opportunity to return to Pasir Mas, Kelantan, more frequently to visit relatives.
“Although my parents have passed away, I still frequently travel to Pasir Mas, Kelantan, to visit my older brother. With the ECRL and the discounts being offered, I will be able to make the trip there even more often.
“At my age, comfort is a higher priority for me… by using the ECRL, I can disembark at the Kota Bharu station and be picked up by a relative to continue to Pasir Mas; this makes my travel arrangements much more convenient,” said the individual, who resides here.
Yesterday, the chief executive officer of Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL), Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak, announced that the Cabinet has approved a 50 per cent discount for children aged two to 12, Malaysian senior citizens aged 60 and above, holders of Persons with Disabilities (OKU) cards, and government retirees.
Additionally, students aged 13 to 24 are eligible for a 40 per cent discount.
The economy-class fare for the ECRL service from Gombak to Kota Bharu, a distance of 523 kilometres reportedly starts as low as RM125 one-way, while the express service for the same route starts at RM147.
For the 378-kilometre journey from Gombak to Kuala Terengganu, the transit fare starts at RM95 one-way, while the express service starts at RM110.
For the 209-kilometre  journey from Gombak to KotaSAS, fares start at RM60 for the transit service and RM68 for the express service. — Bernama

Title: Haze-related school closures subject to joint ministry review, says Fadhlina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Any decision to close schools amid the ongoing haze will be made jointly by the Education Ministry (MOE), Health Ministry (MOH) and the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry (NRES), based on their respective expertise, said Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek.
She said the decision would be based on air quality monitoring and health considerations to ensure students’ safety, while also considering the impact on learning loss if schools were closed for too long.
“From time to time, these three ministries will sit down and make a decision based on the expertise available, particularly at the MOH and NRES levels.
“We hope this will not be prolonged because we know the impact if school closures continue. So it requires a very careful approach and guidance before we make a decision,” she told reporters.
She said this after the Anti-Bullying Literacy programme marking the Anti-Bullying Act 2026, held with the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister’s Department at the Teacher Education Institute (IPG), Bahasa Melayu Campus, today.
Also present was Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan records fewer online crime cases and lower losses
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 20 — Online crime cases in Negeri Sembilan dropped by 268, or 10 per cent, to 2,539 as of September this year, compared with 2,807 cases in the corresponding period last year, while financial losses dropped by RM33.58 million to RM39.86 million.
However, Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said e-commerce fraud cases rose by 24 per cent to 828, compared with 667 in the corresponding period last year, while cases involving non-existent loans increased by 11 per cent to 404 from 365.
“Investment scam cases fell by 20 per cent to 298 from 374, while total losses declined by RM24.50 million, or 66 per cent.
“Phone scam cases also fell by 28 per cent to 784 from 1,095, with losses amounting to RM7.24 million,” he said in a statement here today.
Alzafny attributed the decline in cases and financial losses to public awareness programmes, enforcement efforts and strategic collaborations, particularly those targeting phone scams and investment fraud, which had previously accounted for a significant proportion of cases and losses.
However, he said the increase in e-commerce fraud cases required urgent attention and stronger preventive measures to curb the upward trend.
He advised the public to remain vigilant and verify information before conducting transactions. He also urged them to use available resources, including the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) hotline at 997 and the Semak Mule portal, to help protect themselves from scams. — Bernama

Title: Batu Muda tops API readings as haze worsens in 25 areas across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Twenty-five areas nationwide remained at unhealthy air quality levels as of 4pm today, with Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recording the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 173.
According to the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, five areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy readings: Johan Setia (171), Shah Alam (170), Petaling Jaya (169), Klang (164) and Banting (162).
Three areas in Melaka also recorded unhealthy air quality: Bukit Rambai (166), Alor Gajah (156) and Bandaraya Melaka (156). In Negeri Sembilan, Nilai recorded 165, Seremban 161 and Port Dickson 154.
Meanwhile, in Kuala Lumpur, apart from Baru Muda, Cheras recorded 169 and Putrajaya 164.
In Johor, unhealthy readings were recorded in Larkin (159), Kluang and Pasir Gudang at 156 each, Pengerang and Kota Tinggi at 155 each, and Batu Pahat and Tangkak at 153 each.
Also affected were Paka (155) in Terengganu, and Tasek Ipoh (154), Pegoh Ipoh (151) and Tanjung Malim (114) in Perak.
A total of 35 areas recorded moderate API readings nationwide, while only eight areas had good readings.
API readings of between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal rejects fashion designer Jovian Mandagie’s bid to overturn RM10m payment order
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — The Court of Appeal today dismissed fashion designer Datuk Jovian Mandagie’s appeals to set aside the High Court’s decisions granting two companies’ applications for summary judgment against him in a lawsuit over the alleged breach of friendly loan agreements.
A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, Datuk Seri Mohd Firuz Jaffril and Datin Paduka Evrol Mariette Peters, dismissed the appeal by a 2-1 majority decision.
Justices Wong and Mohd Firuz Jaffril decided the majority decision while Peters dissented.
Lawyer Siti Nur Athirazatti Rohizad, representing Bina Pragmatik Sdn Bhd and Cekap Air Sdn Bhd, confirmed the court’s decision when contacted by Bernama.
In affirming the High Court's decision to enter summary judgment against Jovian, the majority held that the evidential burden rested on him to show the existence of a triable issue, which he had failed to do.
Meanwhile, Peters said Jovian's appeal should be allowed because there was no written documentary evidence setting out the terms of the “friendly loan” at the time the transactions were made.
The court ordered Jovian, who is the former son-in-law of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, to pay RM60,000 in legal costs.
The High Court Judge, Datuk Ahmad Fairuz Zainol Abidin, (now Court of Appeal judge) had allowed Cekap Air and Bina Pragmatik's applications on April 2 and 4, 2024, respectively to enter summary judgment against Jovian and ordered him to pay RM5 million each to the two companies.
The summary judgment was obtained when the court decided the case through written submissions without a full trial.
The two companies had filed separate lawsuits against Jovian for allegedly failing to repay RM5 million each, which was loaned to him based on his friendship with the companies’ directors.
Bina Pragmatik claimed that it had lent Jovian RM5 million at his verbal request on March 25, 2022, by transferring the money to the client account of a law firm representing the fashion designer and that it had to be repaid within a period not exceeding 12 months.
The company claimed that despite making several verbal requests for repayment, Jovian had failed to repay the amount. It said a letter of demand was subsequently issued on April 5, 2023, but the amount remains unpaid, resulting in a financial loss to the company.
Meanwhile, Cekap Air claimed it had granted a RM5 million loan on February 25, 2022, following a verbal request from Jovian, with the amount transferred to the client account of the law firm representing him. The loan was repayable within 12 months.
The company claimed that Jovian had breached the loan agreement and had so far failed to repay or return the money, causing the company to suffer losses.
At the Court of Appeal today, lawyers Mohd Hafiz Mahmund and Aawaisha Pillai represented Jovian while counsel Siti Nur Athirazatti and Muhammad Kausar Mohd Khairi represented the two companies. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected in 12 states, KL this evening, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across 12 states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 6pm today.
In a statement today, MetMalaysia said the adverse weather in the Peninsula would affect the whole of Melaka and eight districts in Johor, namely Kluang, Pontian, Kulai, Johor Bahru, Kota Tinggi, Batu Pahat, Tangkak and Muar.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Kuala Muda, Kulim, Baling, Sik, Padang Terap, Pendang and Pokok Sena, while in Penang, the warning covers Seberang Perai Utara.
The warning also covers several areas in Perak, namely Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Larut Matang and Selama, and in Kelantan, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu and Bachok.
In Terengganu, the areas affected are Hulu Terengganu, Setiu, Dungun, Kemaman and Kuala Nerus, while in Pahang, the warning covers Jerantut, Rompin and Bentong. In Selangor, it covers Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Hulu Langat and Petaling, while in Negeri Sembilan, the affected areas are Jelebu, Seremban, Kuala Pilah, Rembau and Tampin.
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, the affected areas are Kuching (Bau and Kuching), Serian, Sarikei (Sarikei, Maradong and Pakan), Betong (Kabong and Saratok), Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Samarahan, Sri Aman (Pantu and Lingga), Mukah (Daro, Tanjung Manis and Matu), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior (Sipitang, Tambunan, Keningau, Sook, Membakut, Beaufort and Tenom), the West Coast (Ranau, Papar, Penampang, Kota Belud, Kota Kinabalu and Tuaran), Kudat (Kota Marudu) and Sandakan (Telupid). — Bernama

Title: Nilai border control officer’s death: Police record statements from 18 individuals, husband remains in remand until Oct 22
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 20 — Police have recorded statements from 18 individuals to assist in investigations into the death of an officer of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), who was found dead at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters in Nilai last Thursday.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation paper would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor in the near future.
“The suspect, who is the victim’s husband and is in his 30s, remains in remand until October 22 to assist in investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
“Checks also revealed that the man has 16 previous criminal and drug-related records,” he told Bernama here today.
Alzafny said the post-mortem found that the woman died from pressure applied to her neck. The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two to the abdomen and one to the right cheek.
The victim, who was in her 30s, was found dead after she was believed to have been stabbed by her husband at the quarters, reportedly following a misunderstanding.
Police received a report on the incident at 9.30pm after the victim’s husband turned himself in at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported the death. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027 debate: Muhyiddin calls for urban poverty master plan, MP allocation law proposed
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — Issues concerning urban poverty, the allocation of funds for Members of Parliament (MPs), and efforts to strengthen the nation’s healthcare sector were among the topics raised during the policy-level debate on the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin (PN-Pagoh) proposed that the government establish a dedicated master plan to address poverty in urban and semi-urban areas over a five-year period, utilising an integrated approach that involves various ministries.
The former prime minister said the plan should focus on housing, healthcare, employment, education, skills training, and social assistance to ensure that low-income groups also benefit from the nation’s economic development.
“A specific plan must be formulated to ensure that the urban poor gain access to economic and educational opportunities, enabling them to improve their own lives and those of their families through the spillover effects of urban development,” he said.
He added that development planning in major cities such as Kuala Lumpur, Penang, and Johor Bahru must incorporate poverty eradication efforts, particularly by providing economic and educational opportunities for low-income populations.
Meanwhile, Khoo Poay Tiong (PH-Kota Melaka) proposed the enactment of a Parliamentary Constituency Development Allocation Act to ensure that all Members of Parliament, regardless of their political affiliation, receive allocations on an equitable basis.
He said the drafting of the act could be carried out by the Parliamentary Service Council, following the enforcement of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025.
“This is for the benefit of all citizens. I hope that Parliament (the Parliamentary Service Council) can initiate the process of drafting the act,” he said.
Meanwhile, P. Prabakaran (PH-Batu) expressed support for the government’s move to offer permanent positions to over 9,000 contract doctors next year.
However, he emphasised that the government must ensure clearer career paths and sufficient training opportunities, while also addressing the welfare of all healthcare workers specifically regarding their workload and work-life balance.
“At the same time, the public continues to face challenges in obtaining treatment at government health clinics and hospitals, including long waiting times, overcrowding, and difficulties in accessing specialist care.
“Therefore, I suggest that the government assess the need to increase the number of doctors, nurses, and healthcare personnel, based on the local population size and patient load at each healthcare facility,” he said.
Prabakaran added that the government should also focus on hospital bed capacity, the maintenance of medical equipment, and the upgrading of existing facilities, in addition to strengthening primary healthcare services and early disease screening. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak steps up preparations to co-host 2027 SEA Games
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 20 — Sarawak is intensifying preparations to co-host the 2027 SEA Games from September 18 to 29 next year, with promotional activities set to continue across the state, the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly was told today.
Sarawak Minister for Youth, Sports and Entrepreneur Development Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said the promotional activities include a torch run covering all 12 divisions in the state.
He said the initiative would extend the excitement of the Games beyond Kuching and provide communities across the state with an opportunity to be part of the historic event.
“On September 18 this year, Sarawak marked the one-year countdown to SEA Games 2027 with a special ceremony to mark key milestones in our preparations.
“The ceremony also provided an opportunity to introduce the Games to the public and raise awareness of Sarawak’s role as co-host. The official SEA Games Sarawak website was also launched to provide the public and media with information and updates on the Games,” he said when winding up the debate for his ministry.
Abdul Karim said Sarawak will host 18 of the 43 sports at the 2027 SEA Games, with dance sport newly included in the Sarawak cluster.
Meanwhile, commenting on the 2026 Malaysia Games, he said the Sarawak government would award cash incentives of RM15,000 to athletes who won gold medals, RM5,000 to silver medallists and RM3,000 to bronze medallists.
Athletes who broke records would also receive an additional RM1,000 incentive in recognition of their outstanding performances and achievements. — Bernama

Title: Sabah CM: RM150m Nabawan police headquarters, housing project to begin in January 2027
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 20 — The construction of the Nabawan district police headquarters (IPD) and police housing project, with an allocation ceiling of RM150 million, is expected to begin in January 2027, said Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.
He said the infrastructure project aimed to strengthen security capabilities, law enforcement and service delivery to the public, particularly in Nabawan and surrounding areas.
He added that the project must be implemented with integrity and in compliance with the stipulated specifications and standards to ensure maximum benefits for the public and Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel.
“We do not merely want to see this project completed, but also want to ensure that it delivers long-term benefits,” he said in a statement after officiating the groundbreaking ceremony for the Nabawan IPD and police housing project today.
Also present were Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, Sabah State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman and Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun.
Hajiji said the construction of the Nabawan IPD was crucial given the district’s strategic location along the border with Indonesia, which required stronger security capabilities to address cross-border crime and illegal activities.
He said these threats called for integrated, effective and continuous enforcement efforts, including strengthening the PDRM in terms of personnel, infrastructure, operational facilities and administrative systems.
According to Hajiji, the Nabawan police station, established in 1976, currently comes under the administration of the Keningau IPD, although Nabawan has an administrative area of about 6,089 square kilometres.
“Given the size of the administrative area, the need for a more structured policing system suited to current security demands warrants serious attention.
“The development of the Nabawan IPD is an important step towards strengthening the police presence and policing capabilities in the area,” he said.
Hajiji also described the project as a manifestation of the government’s unwavering concern for the welfare, comfort and safety of front-line personnel.
“Providing a conducive infrastructure equipped with the latest technological facilities is no longer a luxury, but a critical necessity, particularly in border areas,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia looks to put durians on the fast track to China by road, rail in three to four days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The government is stepping up negotiations with several countries in the region to facilitate the export of fresh durians to China by road and rail, with shipments expected to take just three to four days, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the initiative was aimed at providing a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to air freight, which is expensive, and sea transport, which takes considerably longer.
He said the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) was working closely with the Foreign Ministry and Transport Ministry to coordinate cross-border routes through Thailand, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia.
“Overland shipments are expected to take only three to four days, allowing goods, particularly durians, to reach the Chinese market quickly. Malaysian durians are very popular among consumers in China, but sometimes they find it difficult to obtain them at more affordable prices,” he said when replying to a supplementary question from Tan Kar Hing (PH-Gopeng).
Mohamad added that formal negotiations to secure transit rights began on July 20 to pave the way for the proposed route through the four countries. — Bernama

Title: States urged to gazette over 15,000ha of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia, FT
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 20 — More than 15,000 hectares or 64.47 per cent of public open spaces in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories have not yet been gazetted or are still in the process of gazettement, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming.
He said all state governments have been urged to expedite the gazettement of public open spaces to ensure designated green areas remain protected and are fully utilised for the benefit of the people, particularly by providing green spaces in densely populated areas.
He said 23,297.15 hectares of public open spaces have been identified in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territories as of December 2025. However, only 35.53 per cent, or 8,278.44 hectares, have been gazetted so far.
“Another 15,018.72 hectares, equivalent to 64.47 per cent, have yet to be gazetted or are still in the process of gazettement. This situation requires attention and follow-up action by state governments to expedite the process in line with the Malaysia Madani sustainable environmental development agenda,” he said in a statement here today.
Nga said public open spaces are not merely areas for leisure and recreation but also important assets that contribute to the well-being of the people.
He said such spaces also serve as green zones that absorb surface runoff, helping to reduce the risk of flash floods, while providing recreational areas that improve the community’s quality of life.
He said gazettement is crucial to protect public open spaces from encroachment, inappropriate changes in land use, as well as management and maintenance issues that could compromise users’ safety.
As such, he called on state governments to intensify gazettement efforts in accordance with Section 62 of the National Land Code [Act 828], as the matter falls under the jurisdiction of state governments.
“The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT), through PLANMalaysia, will continue to monitor the gazettement status of public open spaces in collaboration with relevant parties to support more sustainable, liveable urban development that prioritises the well-being of the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MARA says all 242 sponsored students in France safe amid unrest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Majlis Amanah Rakyat (MARA) is closely monitoring the situation in France to ensure the safety and welfare of its 242 sponsored students amid the unrest.
Its deputy director-general (Education) Zahari Aziz said all 242 students were safe, based on the latest reports from student representatives at their respective universities, and none had been reported to have been involved in the unrest.
“Academic activities are continuing as usual. In areas experiencing public transport disruptions, the universities have taken appropriate measures to conduct classes online,” he said in a statement today.
He said MARA, through its overseas office in Frankfurt, Germany, remained in close contact with the students and had reminded them to stay alert and avoid areas where demonstrations were taking place.
The students had also been advised to follow instructions issued by the local authorities and the Malaysian Embassy in Paris, he said.
“MARA would continue to monitor the situation, with the safety and welfare of its sponsored students remaining a top priority,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Queen calls for long-term measures to protect students from haze
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 20 — Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, has urged the government, private sector and local communities to take proactive, collective action to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families.
Her Majesty stressed the urgent need for a coordinated response, emphasising long-term strategies rather than temporary measures introduced only during haze emergencies.
“Collective action, particularly from the government and private sector, is needed to plan proactive measures to address the physical and psychological effects of haze on students and families.
“Close cooperation from local communities is also essential to strengthen the effectiveness of home-based teaching and learning (PdPR).
“Relevant parties must also develop long-term strategic plans rather than relying solely on temporary solutions when haze emergencies occur,” Her Majesty said.
The royal message was shared in a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook page.
The Queen delivered the message in connection with an audience involving the Johor government, parents and educators on haze-related issues and schooling at the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB) Tower, yesterday.
The session reflected Her Majesty’s concern for the well-being and education of the younger generation.
Her Highness Che’ Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Johor was also present.
In the same message, the Queen also expressed her appreciation to Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah and Jeffrey Cheah Foundation for contributing face masks for schoolchildren in Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Her Majesty also commended Tan Sri Patrick Yeoh and YTL Communications for providing SIM cards to support students’ access to digital learning, and thanked other partners who had contributed to the welfare of schoolchildren.
The audience was also attended by State Secretary Datuk Mohammed Ridha Abd Kadir and State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali.
Representatives from state and federal departments, teachers, parents, Bangsa Johor Bahagia (BJB) residents and People’s Housing Programme (PPR) communities were also present. — Bernama

Title: Govt discusses measures to tackle glut of imported vegetables hurting local farmers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 20 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (MAFS) is in discussions with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (Miti) to find effective measures to address the glut of imported vegetables, which is affecting local producers.
Its minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the discussions also took into account the implementation of the requirement to submit a Certificate of Analysis (CoA), which became mandatory on June 1, 2026, although some views held that the measure was still insufficient.
“We have brought this matter up for discussion at the food security level, and we are analysing what new measures need to be introduced to protect the position of vegetable growers in Malaysia, as well as those involved in fruit production,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a supplementary question from Wong Shu Qi (PH-Kluang) on the need for imported vegetables and fruits to obtain good agricultural practices certification equivalent to Malaysia Good Agricultural Practices Certification Scheme (myGAP), as well as measures to protect local farmers from competition with imported produce that is not subject to the same standards.
Mohamad said imported vegetables and fruits entering Malaysia were currently not required to have good agricultural practices certification equivalent to myGAP in their countries of origin, but remained subject to import requirements, including import permits, phytosanitary certificates issued by exporting countries and inspections by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS).
He said commodities facing oversupply included chillies, cabbage, round cabbage, mustard greens, tomatoes and cucumbers, prompting complaints from local growers, including those in Cameron Highlands and Johor.
In response to Wong’s original question on the performance of myGAP certification since the introduction of e-myGAP in 2020, Mohamad said the system was introduced to shorten the certification period from two years to 90 working days without compromising compliance with Malaysian Standards (MS).
However, he said the timeframe depended on the farm’s level of readiness and the applicant’s compliance with all stipulated certification requirements.
Based on records, Mohamad said the number of applications increased from 2,507 in 2021 to 3,652 in 2025, while 3,282 applications were recorded for 2026 as of the reporting cut-off.
Of these, the number of applications successfully certified in less than 90 working days stood at 324 in 2021, 163 in 2022, 183 in 2023, 373 in 2024, 249 in 2025 and 206 in 2026.
However, he said most applications still took more than 90 working days to process, involving 2,097 applications in 2021, 1,895 in 2022, 3,277 in 2023, 2,967 in 2024 and 3,106 in 2025. This was partly due to the need to carry out corrective actions to address identified non-compliance.
Meanwhile, responding to a supplementary question from Nurul Amin Hamid (PN-Padang Terap) on market preference for myGAP-certified produce and guidance for smallholders, Mohamad said the Department of Agriculture would assist farm operators in obtaining certification once applications had been submitted.
He said the ministry had also asked the Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (FAMA) to intervene in marketing agricultural produce when oversupply caused selling prices to fall below production costs.
“This happens when, for example, the selling prices of chillies, okra or other crops fall too low, below production costs. We then ask Fama to intervene so that farmers and small-scale vegetable growers do not incur losses when there is an oversupply in the market,” he said. — Bernama
